islands.name: Isle of Skye
islands.shortDescription: The largest of the Inner Hebrides, famed for the Cuillin mountains, dramatic coastlines, and the Old Man of Storr.

islands.name: Isle of Mull

islands.name: Isle of Arran

islands.name: Lewis and Harris

islands.name: Isle of Man

islands.name: Islay

islands.name: Mainland (Shetland)
islands.shortDescription: Britain's most northerly large island, closer to Bergen than to Edinburgh, with deep voes, sea cliffs and Up Helly Aa fire festivals.

islands.name: St Kilda (Hirta)
islands.shortDescription: Remote, dual UNESCO World Heritage Site 41 miles west of the Outer Hebrides; evacuated in 1930 and now home only to a small military and conservation team.

islands.name: Isle of Bute
islands.shortDescription: A gentle, accessible Clyde island with the Victorian resort town of Rothesay and the Gothic-revival Mount Stuart House.

islands.name: Mainland (Orkney)
islands.shortDescription: The largest of the Orkney Islands, dense with Neolithic monuments including Skara Brae, Maeshowe and the Ring of Brodgar.

islands.name: Isle of Wight
islands.shortDescription: Diamond-shaped island off Hampshire, famous for the Needles, Osborne House and one of Europe's largest music festivals.

islands.name: Fair Isle
islands.shortDescription: Britain's most remote inhabited island, midway between Orkney and Shetland — famed for knitwear, seabirds, and rare bird sightings.

islands.name: Anglesey (Ynys Môn)
islands.shortDescription: The largest Welsh island, separated from the mainland by the Menai Strait and crossed by Telford's and Stephenson's bridges.

islands.name: Jersey
islands.shortDescription: Largest of the Channel Islands, 14 miles from the French coast — a Crown Dependency with its own parliament and currency.

islands.name: Lundy
islands.shortDescription: Granite island in the Bristol Channel; a marine nature reserve owned by the National Trust and run by the Landmark Trust.

islands.name: Rathlin Island
islands.shortDescription: Northern Ireland's only permanently inhabited offshore island, famed for its seabird colonies and the Robert the Bruce cave.

islands.name: Guernsey

islands.name: Iona
islands.shortDescription: Tiny island off Mull's western tip; the spiritual cradle of Christianity in Scotland and home to Iona Abbey.

islands.name: Inchcailloch
islands.shortDescription: Wooded island in Loch Lomond, part of the Loch Lomond National Nature Reserve, with a circular trail and the ruined chapel of St Kentigerna.

islands.name: Belle Isle (Windermere)
islands.shortDescription: The largest of Windermere's islands and the only one ever permanently inhabited; site of England's first round house, built in 1774.

islands.name: St Mary's (Isles of Scilly)
islands.shortDescription: The largest of the subtropical-feeling Isles of Scilly, 28 miles south-west of Land's End.

islands.name: Staffa
islands.shortDescription: Uninhabited basalt island famed for Fingal's Cave, whose hexagonal columns inspired Mendelssohn's overture.

islands.name: Burgh Island
islands.shortDescription: Tidal island off the South Devon coast, famous for its 1929 art-deco hotel, the haunt of Agatha Christie, Noël Coward and the Beatles.

islands.name: Lindisfarne (Holy Island)
islands.shortDescription: Tidal island off the Northumberland coast, cradle of Celtic Christianity in England and home to the iconic Lindisfarne Castle.

islands.name: Brownsea Island
islands.shortDescription: National Trust island in Poole Harbour, birthplace of the Scout movement and a stronghold for native red squirrels.

islands.name: Isle of Dogs
islands.shortDescription: Peninsula formed by a Thames meander in east London, technically an island since the West India Docks were cut across its neck in 1802; now home to Canary Wharf.

islands.name: Eel Pie Island
islands.shortDescription: Small inhabited island in the Thames at Twickenham, legendary for its 1960s music venue that hosted The Rolling Stones, The Who and Pink Floyd.

islands.name: Linga

islands.shortDescription: Spike Island (Irish: Inis Píc) is an island of 103 acres (42 ha) in Cork Harbour, Ireland. Originally the site of a monastic settlement, the island is dominated by an 18th-century bastion fort now named Fort Mitchel.

islands.shortDescription: Whale Island is a small island in Portsmouth Harbour, close by Portsea Island. It is home to HMS Excellent, the oldest shore training establishment within the Royal Navy, and the location of the Navy Command Headquarters.

islands.name: Salt Island
islands.shortDescription: Salt Island (Welsh: Ynys yr Halen) is joined to Holy Island, Anglesey, in North Wales. It is a natural provider of shelter for the town's Old Harbour from the Irish Sea and is part of the Port of Holyhead.
